title: Debits and Credits
description: Learn the system behind recording accounting transactions.
html:
Debits and credits

Every accounting transaction affects at least two accounts. Debits and credits are the system used to record those changes.

A debit does not automatically mean increase, and a credit does not automatically mean decrease.

Whether a debit increases or decreases an account depends on the type of account.

Total Debits = Total Credits

Easy memory rule

Assets and Expenses normally increase with debits.

Liabilities, Equity, and Revenue normally increase with credits.

Example 1

The owner invests $10,000 cash into the business.

Cash is an asset, so it increases with a debit.

Owner's equity increases with a credit.

Debit Cash $10,000

Credit Equity $10,000

Example 2

The business pays $1,000 rent in cash.

Rent Expense increases with a debit.

Cash decreases with a credit.

Debit Rent Expense $1,000

Credit Cash $1,000

Never forget

  • Every transaction must balance.
  • Total debits must equal total credits.
  • Debit does not mean good or bad.
  • Credit does not mean increase in every account.

quiz.prompt: A company receives $5,000 cash from a customer for services already performed. Which account is credited?
quiz.explanation: Cash increases with a debit, while Service Revenue increases with a credit.
